Simpson’s Rule

Definite integral. No ∫ key. Edit ln(X). Even number of strips.

keys
MODE→6→2

The fx-50FH II has no definite-integral button. This WebCal Simpson listing asks for lower X, upper Y, then even strip count A. The green ln(X) is f(X); change only that (variable must stay X). πr forces cosine into radians so the 4–2–4 Simpson weights work even if SET UP is Deg. For 0→B To A and Next come from SHIFT 3 (P-CMD).

note

61 bytes plus the integrand of the shared 680-byte pool. Create the slot in COMP, Rad if the integrand uses sin/cos/tan. Type ? → : ◢ Goto Lbl If Then from SHIFT 3 (P-CMD).

formula
∫ab​f(x)dx≈(h/3)(y0​+4y1​+2y2​+…+yn​)

Program (one line)

basic
ClrMemory:?→X:?→Y:?→A:A⁻¹(Y−X→Y:For 0→B To A:ln(X:Ans(3−cos(πrB)−(B²=BA)M+:X+Y→X:Next:YM÷3

Example 1: ∫₁² ln x dx, 10 strips

Question: Use this program to solve the case: ∫₁² ln x dx, 10 strips.

Given: Exact value is 2 ln 2 − 1 ≈ 0.386294361.

  1. 1 EXE 2 EXE 10 EXE
  2. Display ≈ 0.386293403

Example 2: Same integral, 2 strips (coarse)

Question: Use this program to solve the case: Same integral, 2 strips (coarse).

Given: Even n is required. Two strips is the coarsest legal run.

  1. 1 EXE 2 EXE 2 EXE
  2. A rougher approximation — use this only to check the listing, not for marks

Example 3 (edge): Change f — here ∫₀¹ e^X dX

Question: Use this program to solve the case: Change f — here ∫₀¹ e^X dX.

Given: Replace ln(X) with e^(X. Lower 0, upper 1, n = 10. Exact e − 1 ≈ 1.718281828.

  1. Edit only the green integrand. Variable stays X
  2. 0 EXE 1 EXE 10 EXE
  3. Odd n is illegal for Simpson: the weights 4-2-4 break
note

πr is π (SHIFT EXP) then the r suffix (SHIFT Ans 2). A⁻¹ is the x⁻¹ key after A. Trigonometric integrands: SET UP Rad. Source: WebCal simpson.htm (61-byte For/Next version).
